claim: Fixing m2 at 0.5, so that force is exactly 0.5/r^2, did not lift the force probe. Final force R2 was 0.750 at layer 1 (seed 14, control 0.560, margin 0.19) and 0.732 at layer 2 (seed 15, control 0.508, margin 0.224). accel_step reached 0.924 and 0.946 at layer 4 (controls 0.743 and 0.762, margins 0.18), a raw R2 lead of 0.17-0.21 over force. Distance was decoded at 0.87-0.89, so the force ceiling of about 0.73-0.75 comes from the 1/r^2 nonlinearity or how the layers encode it, not from m2 information missing from the residual stream.
confidence_note: Both seeds independently meet every expected-if-false criterion by a wide margin: force R2 is at most 0.78 (0.75 and 0.73, inside the 0.65-0.74 band from spread-m2 runs), and accel_step leads by at least 0.12 (0.175 and 0.215). Neither seed approaches the 0.85 force R2 the hypothesis predicted. The main limit is that both runs stopped before 3000 steps. Seed 14 stopped at step 1500 (val_mse_ratio 0.063) and seed 15 at step 2500 (0.0145). The later, better-trained seed has the slightly lower force R2, so more training is unlikely to close a gap of more than 0.1, but this is not proven. Only linear probes were used. A nonlinear or log-target probe that decodes force at 0.85 or higher with m2 fixed would show the ceiling is a linear-readout artifact rather than a representational one, though it would still not support the m2 hypothesis. A full 3000-step run showing force R2 at 0.85 or above would reopen the question.
